title: Etale pullback preserves and reflects associated points of quasi-coherent scheme modules
statement: Let $h:V\to U$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume $U$ and $V$ are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $G$ be any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $h^*G$ be its Zariski tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Use the element-annihilator definition of associated points [def-trf-relative-assassin]. Then for every $v\in V$, with $u=h(v)$, one has $v\in\operatorname{Ass}_V(h^*G)$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ass}_U(G)$. No finite-generation assumption on $G$ and no surjectivity or quasi-compactness assumption on $h$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05FP (flat-lemma-etale-weak-assassin-up-down), combined with Tag 05AR (divisors-lemma-ass-weakly-ass), last sentence, on the two locally Noetherian schemes.

proof.text: Fix $v\in V$ and $u=h(v)$. Choose affine opens $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U$ containing $u$ and $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq h^{-1}(U_0)$ containing $v$. By [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction], $h_0:V_0\to U_0$ is etale. By [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], both $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian. Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ correspond to $v$, and let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ correspond to $u$; then $\mathfrak p=h_0^{\sharp,-1}(\mathfrak q)$ by the spectrum description of an affine scheme morphism.

source.place: Tag 05FP (lemma-etale-weak-assassin-up-down), proof, reduction to affine neighbourhoods; Tag 02GJ (morphisms-lemma-etale-characterize).

proof.text: Put $H=G|_{U_0}$ and $M=\Gamma(U_0,H)$. The restriction $H$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Pullback along an open inclusion is this restriction: the latter is left adjoint to open direct image by that node, as is tensor pullback by [def-pc-module-pullback], so uniqueness of left adjoints identifies them. Pullback composition [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition] therefore gives $(h^*G)|_{V_0}\cong h_0^*H$. The map $h_0$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Apply [new-p4-locally-quasicoherent-affine-pullback-sections] with its target open equal to all of $U_0$: it gives a $B$-linear isomorphism $\Gamma(V_0,h_0^*H)\cong B\otimes_A M$. Also $h^*G$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent].

Apply [lem-trf-etale-weakass-invariance] to $A\to B$, $M$, and $\mathfrak q$ from step 1. It gives $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_B(M\otimes_A B)$ if and only if $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_A(M)$. The flip $m\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes m$, with inverse $b\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes b$, is $B$-linear by the tensor balancing relation. Composing it with step 2 identifies $M\otimes_A B$ with $N=\Gamma(V_0,h^*G)$. A linear isomorphism preserves each element annihilator, and hence preserves weak association. Thus $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_B(N)$ if and only if $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_A(M)$.

Since $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian, the ideals $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$ are finitely generated. Apply [lem-sc-ass-weakass-fg-prime] to $(A,M,\mathfrak p)$ and $(B,N,\mathfrak q)$: step 3 is equivalent to $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(N)$ if and only if $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_A(M)$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-associated-points-primes] to the affine opens $V_0\subseteq V$ and $U_0\subseteq U$, using quasi-coherence from step 2. The two sides are respectively $v\in\operatorname{Ass}_V(h^*G)$ and $u\in\operatorname{Ass}_U(G)$. This proves the claimed equivalence for every $v$. All module inputs above allow arbitrary modules, so no finite generation of $G$ has been used; the neighbourhood choices use no surjectivity or quasi-compactness of $h$.
